item.text: The pinned code uses Redis 8’s newer persistent client ownership model: the main thread accepts and executes, while an assigned I/O thread owns that client’s socket between commands. I’m now validating the two notifier-backed handoffs and the precise read/parse/write callbacks so the diagram distinguishes socket ownership from command execution.

item.text: The core lifecycle is confirmed: for an ordinary eligible client, the main event loop owns the listener and accepts the connection; the selected I/O thread then reads and RESP-parses; the main thread alone runs `processCommand()`; and the same I/O thread flushes the generated reply. The handoffs move the client between per-thread lists under mutexes and wake the other event loop with an event notifier, with socket read/write flags disabled while crossing.
